4	All dependencies are installed. Do not add packages.
5	
6	## Layout
7	
8	| Path | Purpose |
9	|---|---|
10	| `src/main.tsx` | Client entry. Already imports `styles/tokens.css` (design tokens). |
11	| `src/App.tsx` | App shell only: layout, navigation and the route table. No page bodies. |
12	| `src/pages/<Name>Page.tsx` | One file per route. Composes components and hooks; owns the page's loading/empty/error states. |
13	| `src/components/<Name>.tsx` | Reusable UI, one exported component per file. Data in through props, actions out through callbacks; no fetching. |
14	| `src/hooks/use<Name>.ts` | Data loading and stateful UI logic shared by pages. |
15	| `src/api/client.ts` | The only place that calls `fetch`: one typed function per endpoint, using `shared/` types. |
16	| `src/styles/` | `tokens.css` (copied design tokens) plus app styles built only from those tokens. |
17	| `shared/types.ts` | Domain entities and API request/response types shared by client and server. |
18	| `shared/<topic>.ts` | Pure business/validation logic (no I/O), with `<topic>.test.ts` beside it when the brief needs unit tests. No fixed entity names or pricing module is required. |
19	| `server/index.ts` | Boots Express: `GET /api/health`, `POST /api/reset`, `registerRoutes(app)`, unknown `/api/*` → 404 JSON, static `dist/` + SPA fallback. Rarely needs edits. |
20	| `server/routes/index.ts` | `registerRoutes(app)` mounts one router per resource. |
21	| `server/routes/<resource>.ts` | `express.Router()` for one resource. Thin handlers: parse the request, call the service, send status and body. |
22	| `server/services/<resource>.ts` | Store reads/writes and invariants for one resource, reusing `shared/` logic. |
23	| `server/db.ts` | JSON-file store: `readDb<T>()` returns the whole dataset (mutate it, then `writeDb(db)`), `resetDb()` restores the seed. |
24	| `server/data/seed.json` | Resolved domain seed copied from `../requirements/seed.json`. The original optional input stays unchanged. `server/data/db.json` is the live copy. |
25	| `e2e/` | Playwright specs. |
26	| `visual-evidence/` | Desktop/mobile PNGs for each target in `../design/visual-plan.json`, outside `test-results/`. |
27	
28	Create only the folders this product needs: a single-screen tool may have one page and no server resources.
29	Imports between files are extensionless (`import { x } from './db'`).
30	
31	## Code structure
32	
33	- One responsibility per file. Split a file before it passes about 200 lines; never collect every page, component or endpoint in one catch-all file.
34	- Name files and symbols after the product's domain (`BookingCard.tsx`, `routes/bookings.ts`, `shared/pricing.ts`), not `utils`, `helpers` or `misc`.
35	- Keep each rule in one place: calculations and validation in `shared/`, store access in `server/services/`. Components and route handlers call them instead of re-implementing them.
36	- Strict types end to end: no `any`, `@ts-ignore` or non-null assertions to silence errors.
37	- Small functions with intention-revealing names and early returns; named constants instead of repeated literals for statuses and limits.
38	- No dead or commented-out code, unused exports or debug logging.
39	
40	## Commands (run from this directory, one plain command at a time)
41	
42	| Command | What it does |
43	|---|---|
44	| `npm run build` | Type-check (`tsc`) then `vite build` into `dist/` |
45	| `npx vitest run` | Unit tests (`{src,server,shared}/**/*.test.ts(x)`); missing tests fail |
46	| `npx playwright test` | Builds, starts the server on port 3100, runs `e2e/`; add `--grep "<case-id>"` to run one case |
47	| `npm start` | Production server on `PORT` (default 3000) serving API + `dist/` — long-running, do not run it yourself |
48	
49	## Verification contract
50	
51	Keep one Chromium project and one worker: every test resets the same JSON store.
52	Call `POST /api/reset` in `beforeEach`; do not run mutation tests in parallel.
53	Acceptance tests belong in `e2e/case-<id>.spec.ts` with exact IDs from
54	`../requirements/acceptance.json`. Cases can be supplied by the brief or derived
55	from requested behavior when the brief has no explicit tests. Additional tests belong in
56	`journey.spec.ts`, `edge-cases.spec.ts`, `smoke.spec.ts`, and `visual.spec.ts`.
57	Do not change official expected values or hide failures with retries or skips.
58	
59	Read `../requirements/product.json` for the actual roles, entities and primary
60	journey; anonymous and single-screen products are supported. Never introduce
61	an unrelated marketplace, approval flow, money formula or persona switcher.
62	For static presentation with no meaningful pure logic, the reviewed product may
63	set `unit_tests_required: false` and explain `unit_test_reason`; the runner marks
64	unit verification not applicable only if no existing unit files need execution.
65	
66	The desktop viewport is 1440×900. Visual tests also use 390×844 via
67	`page.setViewportSize`, preserving one project and sequential resets. The
68	designer chooses 1–3 representative screens or states in `../design/visual-plan.json`.
69	Capture every target in both sizes as `visual-evidence/{desktop|mobile}-{target.id}.png`.
70	Use `page.screenshot({ path, fullPage: true, animations: 'disabled' })`, attach
71	the PNG with `testInfo.attach`, and wait for actual content and loaded images
72	before capture. Assert no horizontal page overflow. Do not use fixed sleeps.
73	
74	Screenshots support a separate visual review. After polish and final regression,
75	the visual reviewer reads every final planned PNG and records findings in
76	`../quality/visual-review.json`; the runner stamps the review and screenshot
77	and visual-plan hashes in `../quality/evidence.json` so stale evidence cannot pass.

1	# QueueFlow — Requirements
2	
3	## 1. Product and scope
4	**Source brief.** `input/brief.md` holds three sections; the first two (Wheels2Go car rental) are wrapped in HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) and are inactive. The active brief is section `#3` **QueueFlow — Smart Queue & Appointment Management Platform**. Only QueueFlow is specified here.
5	
6	**Users:** customers of service businesses, branch staff at service counters, and administrators. Anonymous visitors may open a large-screen queue display.
7	
8	**Outcome:** a digital queue and appointment platform: customers pick a branch and service, get a walk-in ticket or book an appointment, and track position and estimated wait; staff call and serve in FIFO order; admins manage branches/services/staff and monitor queues and statistics.
9	
10	**Excluded:** real authentication, SMS/e-mail notifications, payments, multi-tenant businesses, ticket priority lanes, deleting branches/services/staff (deactivate/edit only), customer self-registration.
11	
12	**Integrations / prerequisites:** none external. The brief asks for "demo accounts and an easy role-switching mechanism", so a persona switcher is the *explicit* authentication boundary: no passwords. Real-time updates use short polling (the brief allows an "equivalent real-time mechanism"); WebSocket is not required.
13	
14	## 2. Roles and capabilities
15	| Role | Capabilities |
16	|---|---|
17	| visitor | Open public queue display `/display` for a branch (read-only). |
18	| customer | View active branches and active services; generate walk-in ticket; book/cancel appointments; track ticket position/wait; cancel own Waiting/Called ticket; view own history. |
19	| staff | See own branch/counter, queue, current customer; Call Next, Start, Complete, No-Show, Cancel Ticket for tickets at own branch. |
20	| admin | Manage branches, services, staff, counter assignment; monitor all queues; view statistics. |
21	
22	Demo personas (header persona switcher, always visible, keyboard-operable select or menu; selection stored in `localStorage` key `queueflow.userId` and survives refresh; default on first load: Alex Rivera): Alex Rivera, Emma Brown, James Miller (customers); Sarah Johnson, Michael Chen, David Wilson (staff); Jordan Ellis (admin). The client sends `X-User-Id` on every API call; the server enforces role permissions (403 `FORBIDDEN`) and rejects unknown IDs (401 `UNKNOWN_USER`). Each role has its own navigation and landing page: customer `/customer`, staff `/staff`, admin `/admin`, display `/display?branchId=...`.
23	
24	## 3. Functional requirements
25	
26	### Branches and services (admin)
27	- **FR-001** Given admin, when opening Branches, then all branches list name, code, address, hours, counters, offered services, assigned staff, active flag.
28	- **FR-002** Given admin, when creating/editing a branch with name, code (2–4 uppercase letters, unique), address, openTime < closeTime (HH:MM), counterCount 1–20, ≥1 service, then it persists and appears to customers if active. Invalid input shows field errors; the server returns 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Reducing counterCount below an assigned staff member's counter returns 409 `COUNTER_IN_USE`.
29	- **FR-003** Given admin, when creating/editing a service with name, code (2–3 uppercase letters, unique), description, durationMinutes (integer 1–240), category, then it persists. Toggling Active off hides it from customer booking and new tickets; existing tickets are unaffected.
30	- **FR-004** Given admin, when creating/editing staff (name, e-mail unique, branch, optional counter) and assigning a staff member to a counter, then the counter must exist at that branch and not be held by another staff member (409 `COUNTER_TAKEN`); a staff member without a counter cannot Call Next (409 `NO_COUNTER`).
31	
32	### Customer booking and tickets
33	- **FR-005** Given customer, when opening Branches, then active branches show name, address, hours, services and current waiting count.
34	- **FR-006** Given customer, when browsing Services, then active services show name, description, duration, category.
35	- **FR-007** Given customer, when choosing branch → service (only services the branch offers and that are active) → "Walk-in Queue" and confirming, then a ticket with status Waiting and unique number `{branchCode}-{serviceCode}-{seq:3}` is created and shown (TR-1).
36	- **FR-008** Given a branch, when tickets are created on the same business day, then `seq` is the next integer per (branch, service, business date), starting at 1, with no gaps from rapid or duplicated submissions (server-atomic).
37	- **FR-009** Given a customer with an active (Waiting/Called/Serving) ticket for the same branch+service, when generating another, then 409 `DUPLICATE_TICKET` with a clear message and no new ticket. Double-clicking Generate yields one ticket.
38	- **FR-010** Given branch outside operating hours at app time, or inactive branch/service, or service not offered, when generating a ticket, then 409 `BRANCH_CLOSED` / `BRANCH_INACTIVE` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and a message.
39	- **FR-011** Given customer, when opening My Tickets, then each active ticket shows number, branch, service, status badge, position and estimated wait (Waiting), "Proceed to counter N" (Called), "Being served at counter N" (Serving). Data refreshes every ≤2 s automatically (TR-3).
40	- **FR-012** Given customer with Waiting/Called ticket, when clicking Cancel Ticket (with confirm), then status Cancelled and queue positions recompute.
41	- **FR-013** Given customer, when opening History, then own completed/cancelled/no-show tickets and cancelled/converted appointments are listed newest first with status, branch, service and time.
42	
43	### Queue management
44	- **FR-014** Queue scope is the branch: Waiting tickets of one branch are ordered by (`createdAt`, then ticket `id`) ascending; this is the FIFO order across all services of that branch.
45	- **FR-015** Given staff with a counter and no Called/Serving ticket, when clicking Call Next, then the first Waiting ticket at the staff's branch becomes Called with staffId, counterNumber, calledAt (TR-2). If none, 409 `QUEUE_EMPTY`.
46	- **FR-016** Given a staff member with a Called or Serving ticket, when calling next, then 409 `STAFF_BUSY` (one customer at a time). A ticket can only be called from Waiting; concurrent Call Next requests never call the same ticket twice (second call gets the next ticket or `QUEUE_EMPTY`).
47	- **FR-017** Given a Called ticket assigned to this staff, when Start Service, then Serving + startedAt. Given Serving, when Complete Service, then Completed + endedAt. Given Called, when No-Show, then No-Show + endedAt. Cancel Ticket is allowed on Waiting (same branch), Called or Serving tickets and sets Cancelled + endedAt. Other transitions return 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`. Staff of another branch get 403.
48	- **FR-018** Given any ticket leaves Waiting (called, cancelled, completed), then positions/estimates of all remaining Waiting tickets are recomputed from live data on each read (TR-4).
49	- **FR-019** Position and estimate (see §5): position = 1 + Waiting tickets ahead; estimatedWaitMinutes = sum of `durationMinutes` of the services of the tickets ahead.
50	
51	### Staff dashboard
52	- **FR-020** Given staff, when opening dashboard, then it shows assigned branch and counter, current customer (Called/Serving ticket with number, customer, service), waiting count at branch, next customer (first Waiting), completed services today by this staff, average service duration today by this staff (1 decimal minutes, "—" if none), and the waiting list grouped/labelled by service.
53	- **FR-021** Buttons Call Next, Start Service, Complete Service, No-Show, Cancel Ticket are shown, disabled with a visible reason when not applicable, and each updates shared state immediately and the screen within ≤2 s polling.
54	
55	### Appointments
56	- **FR-022** Given customer, when choosing branch, service and a date (today to today+14 days) then slots are listed: every 30 min from openTime where start + durationMinutes ≤ closeTime. A slot is Available if at least one counter with an assigned staff member has no overlapping Scheduled appointment; otherwise shown Unavailable (disabled). Past slots (start < app now) are not shown as bookable.
57	- **FR-023** Given a slot, when booking, then an Appointment (Scheduled) is created and assigned to the lowest-numbered free counter and its staff. Past date/time → 400 `PAST_DATE`; a slot with no free counter (same counter/staff overlap) → 409 `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`; the same customer already holding an overlapping Scheduled appointment → 409 `DUPLICATE_APPOINTMENT` (TR-5).
58	- **FR-024** Given customer, when clicking Cancel on an upcoming Scheduled appointment, then status Cancelled and its slot is available again. Converted/cancelled appointments cannot be cancelled (409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`).
59	- **FR-025** Given app time reaches a Scheduled appointment's start (date+startTime), then the server (on each request and at least every 5 s) converts it exactly once into a Waiting `appointment`-type ticket with `createdAt` = appointment start, next sequence number, linked `appointmentId`, and sets appointment status Converted with `ticketId`. Conversion ignores FR-009 and FR-010 (not blocked by duplicates or closing).
60	
61	### Real-time, display, admin
62	- **FR-026** Given customer, staff, admin and display views open, when queue state changes, then each view reflects it within ≤2 s without reload (polling `Cache-Control: no-store`).
63	- **FR-027** Given visitor, when opening `/display?branchId=X` (branch selector if omitted), then a large-type screen shows "Now calling" (Called/Serving: ticket number + counter) and the next ≥5 Waiting ticket numbers, readable at 1080p and usable at 360px.
64	- **FR-028** Given admin, when opening Dashboard, then cards show (business date "today" = app clock UTC date): Total customers today (tickets created today), Waiting, Being served (status Serving), Called, Completed, Cancelled, No-Show, Avg waiting time, Avg service duration; plus charts: tickets by status and branch comparison (per branch Completed/Waiting/Cancelled bars, avg wait, avg service). Charts have text/table alternatives.
65	- **FR-029** Given admin, when opening Monitor, then all tickets of the day for all branches are listed with branch filter, status badge, counter, staff; counts update per FR-026.
66	- **FR-030** Given admin, when clicking "Advance demo clock" (15/60 min), then app time moves forward, due appointments convert (FR-025), and every view uses the new time. Reset restores offset 0.
67	
68	### Persistence and validation
69	- **FR-031** All entities persist server-side and survive browser refresh and server restart; `POST /api/reset` restores seed exactly.
70	- **FR-032** Every mutation validates input and returns the error shape in §6; the UI shows the message in an alert region and keeps entered form values.
71	
72	## 4. Domain model
73	All timestamps ISO-8601 UTC strings; dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; times `HH:MM`. Branch-local time = UTC (assumption).
74	- **User**: id, name, email (unique), role `customer|staff|admin`, branchId (staff only, else null), counterNumber (staff only, int|null).
75	- **Branch**: id, name (unique, required), code, address, openTime, closeTime, counterCount (1–20), serviceIds[], isActive.
76	- **Service**: id, name (unique), code, description, durationMinutes (1–240), category, isActive.
77	- **Ticket**: id, ticketNumber, branchId, serviceId, customerId|null (null = walk-in guest created by kiosk, seed only), customerName, type `walk_in|appointment`, businessDate, sequence, status `waiting|called|serving|completed|cancelled|no_show`, createdAt, calledAt|null, startedAt|null, endedAt|null, counterNumber|null, staffId|null, appointmentId|null.
78	- **Appointment**: id, customerId, branchId, serviceId, date, startTime, endTime (= start + service duration), counterNumber, staffId|null, status `scheduled|cancelled|converted`, ticketId|null, createdAt.
79	- **Clock** (seed): `anchorIso`; app now = anchor + real elapsed time since server start/reset + advanced minutes.
80	- Relationships: Branch↔Service many-to-many via serviceIds; User(staff)→Branch; Ticket→Branch/Service/User; Appointment→Ticket (0..1).
81	- Status labels in UI: Waiting, Called, Serving, Completed, Cancelled, No-Show (each with distinct colour **and** text/icon).
82	
83	## 5. Business rules
84	**Ticket status transitions (actor):** waiting→called (staff Call Next); called→serving (assigned staff); serving→completed (assigned staff); called→no_show (assigned staff); waiting|called→cancelled (customer owner or staff of branch); serving→cancelled (staff); waiting→cancelled (staff of branch). Terminal: completed, cancelled, no_show. Admin has read-only access to tickets. "Assigned staff" = ticket.staffId.
85	
86	**Ticket numbering:** `ticketNumber = branch.code + "-" + service.code + "-" + zero-pad(seq,3)`. seq = 1 + max seq among tickets with same branch, service, businessDate (including cancelled). Example: seed has CEN-GC-001..004 → next CEN-GC-005; first CEN-DV ticket of 2026-11-02 is CEN-DV-001.
87	
88	**Business date** = UTC date of app now. Operating hours: open if openTime ≤ time-of-day < closeTime.
89	
90	**Position and wait:** for Waiting ticket T at branch B, ahead = Waiting tickets at B ordered before T in FIFO order. position = |ahead|+1; estimatedWaitMinutes = Σ service.durationMinutes over ahead. Called/Serving/terminal tickets have position null, wait 0/null. Counters count is not used in the estimate (simplification). Worked example (seed): Central waiting = CEN-GC-003 (Tom, 09:40) and CEN-DV-002 (Omar, 09:50). Tom: position 1, wait 0. Omar: position 2, wait 15 (GC duration). After Tom is called → Omar position 1, wait 0. If a new CEN-CS ticket is created: position 3, wait 15+10 = 25. Downtown: DWN-GC-003 (Alex) position 1, wait 0.
91	
92	**Average figures** (rounded half-up to 1 decimal, minutes = ms/60000): avg waiting = mean(startedAt − createdAt) over tickets with startedAt today; avg service = mean(endedAt − startedAt) over Completed tickets today. Seed day: avg waiting = (6+8+20+17+2+30)/6 = 13.8; avg service = (13+9+12)/3 = 11.3. Central: wait 12.8, service 11.0; Downtown: wait 16.0, service 12.0. Staff (seed): Sarah 1 completed avg 13.0; Michael 1 avg 9.0; David 1 avg 12.0. Total customers today = tickets with businessDate today = 11; waiting 3, serving 3, called 0, completed 3, cancelled 1, no-show 1.
93	
94	**Slot overlap:** intervals [start, end) conflict iff s1 < e2 and s2 < e1; touching is allowed. Example Downtown (1 counter): Support (20 min) booked 15:00–15:20 (seed appt_002) blocks a General Consultation (15 min) booking at 15:00 but not at 15:30; at Central (2 counters) Document Verification 2026-11-02 11:00 already uses counter 1, so one more 11:00 booking succeeds on counter 2 and a third fails.
95	
96	**Date rules:** bookable dates today..today+14 (app clock). A slot is past if its start < app now.
97	
98	**Unit-testable pure logic:** ticket numbering, FIFO ordering, position/wait calculation, transition validity, slot generation, overlap detection, counter assignment, statistics/average rounding. Put these in a pure module with Vitest/Node tests.
99	
100	## 6. API and persistence contract
101	JSON; error shape `{ "error": { "code": "STRING", "message": "Human readable" } }`; statuses 400 validation, 401, 403, 404 `NOT_FOUND`, 409 conflicts. Mutations are serialized server-side. Persistent store: server-side file/DB; boot loads `requirements/seed.json` shape (resolved seed) if no store exists. Shared TypeScript types for entities in §4 are used by client and server. Computed Ticket view adds `position`, `estimatedWaitMinutes`, `branchName`, `serviceName`, `staffName`.
102	
103	Infrastructure: `GET /api/health` → `{ "ok": true }`. `POST /api/reset` → restores seed exactly (incl. clock anchor re-based to now, offset 0) → `{ "ok": true }`.
104	
105	| Endpoint | Role | Notes |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `GET /api/users` | any | demo accounts for switcher |
108	| `GET /api/branches` | any | includes `staff[]`, `waitingCount`; customers receive only active |
109	| `POST /api/branches`, `PUT /api/branches/:id` | admin | FR-002 |
110	| `GET /api/services`, `POST /api/services`, `PUT /api/services/:id` | read any / write admin | FR-003 |

# QueueFlow — Requirements

## 1. Product and scope
**Source brief.** `input/brief.md` holds three sections; the first two (Wheels2Go car rental) are wrapped in HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) and are inactive. The active brief is section `#3` **QueueFlow — Smart Queue & Appointment Management Platform**. Only QueueFlow is specified here.

**Users:** customers of service businesses, branch staff at service counters, and administrators. Anonymous visitors may open a large-screen queue display.

**Outcome:** a digital queue and appointment platform: customers pick a branch and service, get a walk-in ticket or book an appointment, and track position and estimated wait; staff call and serve in FIFO order; admins manage branches/services/staff and monitor queues and statistics.

**Excluded:** real authentication, SMS/e-mail notifications, payments, multi-tenant businesses, ticket priority lanes, deleting branches/services/staff (deactivate/edit only), customer self-registration.

**Integrations / prerequisites:** none external. The brief asks for "demo accounts and an easy role-switching mechanism", so a persona switcher is the *explicit* authentication boundary: no passwords. Real-time updates use short polling (the brief allows an "equivalent real-time mechanism"); WebSocket is not required.

## 2. Roles and capabilities
| Role | Capabilities |
|---|---|
| visitor | Open public queue display `/display` for a branch (read-only). |
| customer | View active branches and active services; generate walk-in ticket; book/cancel appointments; track ticket position/wait; cancel own Waiting/Called ticket; view own history. |
| staff | See own branch/counter, queue, current customer; Call Next, Start, Complete, No-Show, Cancel Ticket for tickets at own branch. |
| admin | Manage branches, services, staff, counter assignment; monitor all queues; view statistics. |

Demo personas (header persona switcher, always visible, keyboard-operable select or menu; selection stored in `localStorage` key `queueflow.userId` and survives refresh; default on first load: Alex Rivera): Alex Rivera, Emma Brown, James Miller (customers); Sarah Johnson, Michael Chen, David Wilson (staff); Jordan Ellis (admin). The client sends `X-User-Id` on every API call; the server enforces role permissions (403 `FORBIDDEN`) and rejects unknown IDs (401 `UNKNOWN_USER`). Each role has its own navigation and landing page: customer `/customer`, staff `/staff`, admin `/admin`, display `/display?branchId=...`.

## 3. Functional requirements

### Branches and services (admin)
- **FR-001** Given admin, when opening Branches, then all branches list name, code, address, hours, counters, offered services, assigned staff, active flag.
- **FR-002** Given admin, when creating/editing a branch with name, code (2–4 uppercase letters, unique), address, openTime < closeTime (HH:MM), counterCount 1–20, ≥1 service, then it persists and appears to customers if active. Invalid input shows field errors; the server returns 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Reducing counterCount below an assigned staff member's counter returns 409 `COUNTER_IN_USE`.
- **FR-003** Given admin, when creating/editing a service with name, code (2–3 uppercase letters, unique), description, durationMinutes (integer 1–240), category, then it persists. Toggling Active off hides it from customer booking and new tickets; existing tickets are unaffected.
- **FR-004** Given admin, when creating/editing staff (name, e-mail unique, branch, optional counter) and assigning a staff member to a counter, then the counter must exist at that branch and not be held by another staff member (409 `COUNTER_TAKEN`); a staff member without a counter cannot Call Next (409 `NO_COUNTER`).

### Customer booking and tickets
- **FR-005** Given customer, when opening Branches, then active branches show name, address, hours, services and current waiting count.
- **FR-006** Given customer, when browsing Services, then active services show name, description, duration, category.
- **FR-007** Given customer, when choosing branch → service (only services the branch offers and that are active) → "Walk-in Queue" and confirming, then a ticket with status Waiting and unique number `{branchCode}-{serviceCode}-{seq:3}` is created and shown (TR-1).
- **FR-008** Given a branch, when tickets are created on the same business day, then `seq` is the next integer per (branch, service, business date), starting at 1, with no gaps from rapid or duplicated submissions (server-atomic).
- **FR-009** Given a customer with an active (Waiting/Called/Serving) ticket for the same branch+service, when generating another, then 409 `DUPLICATE_TICKET` with a clear message and no new ticket. Double-clicking Generate yields one ticket.
- **FR-010** Given branch outside operating hours at app time, or inactive branch/service, or service not offered, when generating a ticket, then 409 `BRANCH_CLOSED` / `BRANCH_INACTIVE` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and a message.
- **FR-011** Given customer, when opening My Tickets, then each active ticket shows number, branch, service, status badge, position and estimated wait (Waiting), "Proceed to counter N" (Called), "Being served at counter N" (Serving). Data refreshes every ≤2 s automatically (TR-3).
- **FR-012** Given customer with Waiting/Called ticket, when clicking Cancel Ticket (with confirm), then status Cancelled and queue positions recompute.
- **FR-013** Given customer, when opening History, then own completed/cancelled/no-show tickets and cancelled/converted appointments are listed newest first with status, branch, service and time.

### Queue management
- **FR-014** Queue scope is the branch: Waiting tickets of one branch are ordered by (`createdAt`, then ticket `id`) ascending; this is the FIFO order across all services of that branch.
- **FR-015** Given staff with a counter and no Called/Serving ticket, when clicking Call Next, then the first Waiting ticket at the staff's branch becomes Called with staffId, counterNumber, calledAt (TR-2). If none, 409 `QUEUE_EMPTY`.
- **FR-016** Given a staff member with a Called or Serving ticket, when calling next, then 409 `STAFF_BUSY` (one customer at a time). A ticket can only be called from Waiting; concurrent Call Next requests never call the same ticket twice (second call gets the next ticket or `QUEUE_EMPTY`).
- **FR-017** Given a Called ticket assigned to this staff, when Start Service, then Serving + startedAt. Given Serving, when Complete Service, then Completed + endedAt. Given Called, when No-Show, then No-Show + endedAt. Cancel Ticket is allowed on Waiting (same branch), Called or Serving tickets and sets Cancelled + endedAt. Other transitions return 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`. Staff of another branch get 403.
- **FR-018** Given any ticket leaves Waiting (called, cancelled, completed), then positions/estimates of all remaining Waiting tickets are recomputed from live data on each read (TR-4).
- **FR-019** Position and estimate (see §5): position = 1 + Waiting tickets ahead; estimatedWaitMinutes = sum of `durationMinutes` of the services of the tickets ahead.

### Staff dashboard
- **FR-020** Given staff, when opening dashboard, then it shows assigned branch and counter, current customer (Called/Serving ticket with number, customer, service), waiting count at branch, next customer (first Waiting), completed services today by this staff, average service duration today by this staff (1 decimal minutes, "—" if none), and the waiting list grouped/labelled by service.
- **FR-021** Buttons Call Next, Start Service, Complete Service, No-Show, Cancel Ticket are shown, disabled with a visible reason when not applicable, and each updates shared state immediately and the screen within ≤2 s polling.

### Appointments
- **FR-022** Given customer, when choosing branch, service and a date (today to today+14 days) then slots are listed: every 30 min from openTime where start + durationMinutes ≤ closeTime. A slot is Available if at least one counter with an assigned staff member has no overlapping Scheduled appointment; otherwise shown Unavailable (disabled). Past slots (start < app now) are not shown as bookable.
- **FR-023** Given a slot, when booking, then an Appointment (Scheduled) is created and assigned to the lowest-numbered free counter and its staff. Past date/time → 400 `PAST_DATE`; a slot with no free counter (same counter/staff overlap) → 409 `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`; the same customer already holding an overlapping Scheduled appointment → 409 `DUPLICATE_APPOINTMENT` (TR-5).
- **FR-024** Given customer, when clicking Cancel on an upcoming Scheduled appointment, then status Cancelled and its slot is available again. Converted/cancelled appointments cannot be cancelled (409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`).
- **FR-025** Given app time reaches a Scheduled appointment's start (date+startTime), then the server (on each request and at least every 5 s) converts it exactly once into a Waiting `appointment`-type ticket with `createdAt` = appointment start, next sequence number, linked `appointmentId`, and sets appointment status Converted with `ticketId`. Conversion ignores FR-009 and FR-010 (not blocked by duplicates or closing).

### Real-time, display, admin
- **FR-026** Given customer, staff, admin and display views open, when queue state changes, then each view reflects it within ≤2 s without reload (polling `Cache-Control: no-store`).
- **FR-027** Given visitor, when opening `/display?branchId=X` (branch selector if omitted), then a large-type screen shows "Now calling" (Called/Serving: ticket number + counter) and the next ≥5 Waiting ticket numbers, readable at 1080p and usable at 360px.
- **FR-028** Given admin, when opening Dashboard, then cards show (business date "today" = app clock UTC date): Total customers today (tickets created today), Waiting, Being served (status Serving), Called, Completed, Cancelled, No-Show, Avg waiting time, Avg service duration; plus charts: tickets by status and branch comparison (per branch Completed/Waiting/Cancelled bars, avg wait, avg service). Charts have text/table alternatives.
- **FR-029** Given admin, when opening Monitor, then all tickets of the day for all branches are listed with branch filter, status badge, counter, staff; counts update per FR-026.
- **FR-030** Given admin, when clicking "Advance demo clock" (15/60 min), then app time moves forward, due appointments convert (FR-025), and every view uses the new time. Reset restores offset 0.

### Persistence and validation
- **FR-031** All entities persist server-side and survive browser refresh and server restart; `POST /api/reset` restores seed exactly.
- **FR-032** Every mutation validates input and returns the error shape in §6; the UI shows the message in an alert region and keeps entered form values.

## 4. Domain model
All timestamps ISO-8601 UTC strings; dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; times `HH:MM`. Branch-local time = UTC (assumption).
- **User**: id, name, email (unique), role `customer|staff|admin`, branchId (staff only, else null), counterNumber (staff only, int|null).
- **Branch**: id, name (unique, required), code, address, openTime, closeTime, counterCount (1–20), serviceIds[], isActive.
- **Service**: id, name (unique), code, description, durationMinutes (1–240), category, isActive.
- **Ticket**: id, ticketNumber, branchId, serviceId, customerId|null (null = walk-in guest created by kiosk, seed only), customerName, type `walk_in|appointment`, businessDate, sequence, status `waiting|called|serving|completed|cancelled|no_show`, createdAt, calledAt|null, startedAt|null, endedAt|null, counterNumber|null, staffId|null, appointmentId|null.
- **Appointment**: id, customerId, branchId, serviceId, date, startTime, endTime (= start + service duration), counterNumber, staffId|null, status `scheduled|cancelled|converted`, ticketId|null, createdAt.
- **Clock** (seed): `anchorIso`; app now = anchor + real elapsed time since server start/reset + advanced minutes.
- Relationships: Branch↔Service many-to-many via serviceIds; User(staff)→Branch; Ticket→Branch/Service/User; Appointment→Ticket (0..1).
- Status labels in UI: Waiting, Called, Serving, Completed, Cancelled, No-Show (each with distinct colour **and** text/icon).

## 5. Business rules
**Ticket status transitions (actor):** waiting→called (staff Call Next); called→serving (assigned staff); serving→completed (assigned staff); called→no_show (assigned staff); waiting|called→cancelled (customer owner or staff of branch); serving→cancelled (staff); waiting→cancelled (staff of branch). Terminal: completed, cancelled, no_show. Admin has read-only access to tickets. "Assigned staff" = ticket.staffId.

**Ticket numbering:** `ticketNumber = branch.code + "-" + service.code + "-" + zero-pad(seq,3)`. seq = 1 + max seq among tickets with same branch, service, businessDate (including cancelled). Example: seed has CEN-GC-001..004 → next CEN-GC-005; first CEN-DV ticket of 2026-11-02 is CEN-DV-001.

**Business date** = UTC date of app now. Operating hours: open if openTime ≤ time-of-day < closeTime.

**Position and wait:** for Waiting ticket T at branch B, ahead = Waiting tickets at B ordered before T in FIFO order. position = |ahead|+1; estimatedWaitMinutes = Σ service.durationMinutes over ahead. Called/Serving/terminal tickets have position null, wait 0/null. Counters count is not used in the estimate (simplification). Worked example (seed): Central waiting = CEN-GC-003 (Tom, 09:40) and CEN-DV-002 (Omar, 09:50). Tom: position 1, wait 0. Omar: position 2, wait 15 (GC duration). After Tom is called → Omar position 1, wait 0. If a new CEN-CS ticket is created: position 3, wait 15+10 = 25. Downtown: DWN-GC-003 (Alex) position 1, wait 0.

5. App clock is anchored at 2026-11-01T10:00:00Z and runs in real time so seed data is always "today"; admin can advance it. Tests pick slots from UI at execution time.
6. Staff serve all services their branch offers; queue is FIFO per branch across services; estimate ignores counter count and remaining time of in-progress services.
7. Admin was not in the brief's seed list; one admin account was added.
8. Customers without a seeded ticket for a branch+service can create one; seed guest tickets are walk-ins without accounts.
9. Appointment length equals service duration; slot grid is 30 min; slots are assigned to the lowest free counter automatically.
10. Unit tests required: the queue algorithm, estimates, slot/overlap logic and statistics are pure logic (§5).

3	Active brief: section `#3` QueueFlow (Wheels2Go sections are commented out and ignored). Tokens: `design/tokens.json` / `design/tokens.css` (imported directly by the app). All colours, spacing, radii below refer to token names.
4	
5	## 1. Visual direction
6	"Calm operations console": minimal SaaS dashboard, light neutral canvas (`--color-bg`) with white cards (`--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, 1px `--color-border`), a dark navy sidebar/topbar (`--color-nav-bg`) and a single teal accent (`--color-primary`) for primary buttons, active nav and links. Ticket numbers use `--font-mono`, bold. Spacing in `--space-*`; card padding `--space-5` (desktop) / `--space-4` (mobile); gap between cards `--space-4`. One primary action per card (filled teal), secondary = outlined, destructive = outlined/filled with `--color-danger`.
7	
8	Status badges (pill, `--radius-pill`, `--font-size-sm`, medium weight) always show **icon + text**, never colour alone:
9	Waiting ◔ (`status-waiting`), Called ▲ (`status-called`), Serving ● (`status-serving`), Completed ✓ (`status-completed`), Cancelled ✕ (`status-cancelled`), No-Show ⊘ (`status-no-show`). Badge text is exactly: `Waiting`, `Called`, `Serving`, `Completed`, `Cancelled`, `No-Show`. Appointment badges: `Scheduled`, `Cancelled`, `Converted`.
10	
11	No imagery. Do not invent trust claims or integrations.
12	
13	## 2. App shell
14	- **Topbar** (all authenticated screens, sticky, height 56px, `--color-nav-bg`): brand "QueueFlow" (left), demo clock `UTC HH:MM` (`clock-now`), and the **persona switcher** (right): a labelled native `<select>` "Demo account" (`persona-switcher`) listing 7 users as `Name — Role` (e.g. `Emma Brown — Customer`), option value = user id (`usr_202`…). Changing it stores `queueflow.userId`, and navigates to the role landing page (`/customer`, `/staff`, `/admin`). Next to it `current-user` shows `Emma Brown · Customer`. A visible notice "Demo accounts – no passwords" is in the footer.
15	- **Navigation** per role: sidebar 232px (`--width-sidebar`) on ≥1024px; below 1024px a horizontally scrollable-free tab bar under the topbar that wraps (flex-wrap) into up to 2 rows; every item min 44px tall. Active item = `--color-nav-active-bg` + `aria-current="page"`.
16	  - Customer: `nav-book` "Book" → `/customer`; `nav-services` "Services" → `/customer/services`; `nav-tickets` "My Tickets" → `/customer/tickets`; `nav-history` "History" → `/customer/history`.
17	  - Staff: `nav-desk` "Queue Desk" → `/staff`; `nav-display` "Queue Display" → `/display?branchId=<own branch>`.
18	  - Admin: `nav-dashboard` "Dashboard" → `/admin`; `nav-monitor` "Monitor" → `/admin/monitor`; `nav-branches` "Branches" → `/admin/branches`; `nav-services-admin` "Services" → `/admin/services`; `nav-staff-admin` "Staff" → `/admin/staff`.
19	- **Content**: max width `--width-content` (1200px), centred, padding `--space-5` (≥768px) / `--space-4`. Forms max `--width-form`.
20	- **Footer**: `demo-reset` button "Reset demo data" (confirm dialog → `POST /api/reset`, then reload data) and the "Demo accounts" note.
21	- **Display screen `/display`** is public: no sidebar and no persona switcher; a minimal dark header with branch name.
22	- Unknown route → "Page not found" with link to role landing page. Opening a route of another role (e.g. customer at `/admin`) shows `forbidden-state` "You don't have access to this page" with a link to the role's landing page (no API data requested).
23	- Global feedback: `toast` (role="status", aria-live polite, bottom-centre, auto-dismiss 5s, success tone) and per-form `form-error` (role="alert", `--color-danger` on `--color-danger-bg`, with icon) placed at the top of the form/card where the action occurred; entered values are kept. Every data view has loading (`loading-state`, skeleton or "Loading…" with `aria-busy`), empty and error (`error-state` with `retry` button "Retry") states. Buttons disable and show "…" while a request is in flight.
24	- Dialogs (`confirm-dialog`, role="dialog" aria-modal, width `--width-dialog`, focus trapped, Esc = cancel): title, message, `confirm-yes` (label "Confirm"), `confirm-no` (label "Keep").
25	- Time formatting: `HH:MM` (24h UTC). Durations: `15 min`. Dates `YYYY-MM-DD`. Counter: `Counter 2`.
26	
27	## 3. Screens and states
28	
29	### 3.1 `/customer` — Book (customer)
30	Purpose: see branches, generate walk-in ticket or book appointment.
31	- **Desktop 1440×900**: sidebar + content (1200). Top row: page title "Book a visit". Below, a 2-column grid: left (flex 1) list of `branch-card`s (one per active branch: name, address, hours `09:00–17:00`, offered services as chips, `branch-waiting-count` "3 waiting"); right (width `--width-form`) the booking card. Selecting a branch card also sets the form's branch.
32	- **Mobile 390×844**: single column: booking card first, branch cards below.
33	- Booking card fields in order: Branch select, Service select (only active services offered by the branch; disabled until branch chosen), mode radio group "Visit type": "Walk-in Queue" / "Scheduled Appointment"; when appointment: Date input and slot grid (3 columns desktop, 2 columns ≤480px); primary button.
34	- Success (walk-in): the card swaps to `ticket-result` (large mono ticket number, status badge, position, wait, buttons "View My Tickets" → `/customer/tickets` and "Book another"). Success (appointment): toast "Appointment booked for YYYY-MM-DD at HH:MM" and `appointment-result` card with date, time, counter; slot list refreshes.
35	- Errors via `form-error` using the server message (e.g. closed, duplicate, slot unavailable, past date). Empty: "No branches available" / "No available slots".
36	
37	### 3.2 `/customer/services`

# QueueFlow — UI Spec

Active brief: section `#3` QueueFlow (Wheels2Go sections are commented out and ignored). Tokens: `design/tokens.json` / `design/tokens.css` (imported directly by the app). All colours, spacing, radii below refer to token names.

## 1. Visual direction
"Calm operations console": minimal SaaS dashboard, light neutral canvas (`--color-bg`) with white cards (`--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, 1px `--color-border`), a dark navy sidebar/topbar (`--color-nav-bg`) and a single teal accent (`--color-primary`) for primary buttons, active nav and links. System font only. Hierarchy: page title `--font-size-xl` bold; card titles `--font-size-lg`; body `--font-size-md`; meta `--font-size-sm` in `--color-text-muted`. Ticket numbers use `--font-mono`, bold. Spacing in `--space-*`; card padding `--space-5` (desktop) / `--space-4` (mobile); gap between cards `--space-4`. One primary action per card (filled teal), secondary = outlined, destructive = outlined/filled with `--color-danger`.

Status badges (pill, `--radius-pill`, `--font-size-sm`, medium weight) always show **icon + text**, never colour alone:
Waiting ◔ (`status-waiting`), Called ▲ (`status-called`), Serving ● (`status-serving`), Completed ✓ (`status-completed`), Cancelled ✕ (`status-cancelled`), No-Show ⊘ (`status-no-show`). Badge text is exactly: `Waiting`, `Called`, `Serving`, `Completed`, `Cancelled`, `No-Show`. Appointment badges: `Scheduled`, `Cancelled`, `Converted`.

No imagery. Do not invent trust claims or integrations.

## 2. App shell
- **Topbar** (all authenticated screens, sticky, height 56px, `--color-nav-bg`): brand "QueueFlow" (left), demo clock `UTC HH:MM` (`clock-now`), and the **persona switcher** (right): a labelled native `<select>` "Demo account" (`persona-switcher`) listing 7 users as `Name — Role` (e.g. `Emma Brown — Customer`), option value = user id (`usr_202`…). Changing it stores `queueflow.userId`, and navigates to the role landing page (`/customer`, `/staff`, `/admin`). Next to it `current-user` shows `Emma Brown · Customer`. A visible notice "Demo accounts – no passwords" is in the footer.
- **Navigation** per role: sidebar 232px (`--width-sidebar`) on ≥1024px; below 1024px a horizontally scrollable-free tab bar under the topbar that wraps (flex-wrap) into up to 2 rows; every item min 44px tall. Active item = `--color-nav-active-bg` + `aria-current="page"`.
  - Customer: `nav-book` "Book" → `/customer`; `nav-services` "Services" → `/customer/services`; `nav-tickets` "My Tickets" → `/customer/tickets`; `nav-history` "History" → `/customer/history`.
  - Staff: `nav-desk` "Queue Desk" → `/staff`; `nav-display` "Queue Display" → `/display?branchId=<own branch>`.
  - Admin: `nav-dashboard` "Dashboard" → `/admin`; `nav-monitor` "Monitor" → `/admin/monitor`; `nav-branches` "Branches" → `/admin/branches`; `nav-services-admin` "Services" → `/admin/services`; `nav-staff-admin` "Staff" → `/admin/staff`.
- **Content**: max width `--width-content` (1200px), centred, padding `--space-5` (≥768px) / `--space-4`. Forms max `--width-form`.
- **Footer**: `demo-reset` button "Reset demo data" (confirm dialog → `POST /api/reset`, then reload data) and the "Demo accounts" note.
- **Display screen `/display`** is public: no sidebar and no persona switcher; a minimal dark header with branch name.
- Unknown route → "Page not found" with link to role landing page. Opening a route of another role (e.g. customer at `/admin`) shows `forbidden-state` "You don't have access to this page" with a link to the role's landing page (no API data requested).
- Global feedback: `toast` (role="status", aria-live polite, bottom-centre, auto-dismiss 5s, success tone) and per-form `form-error` (role="alert", `--color-danger` on `--color-danger-bg`, with icon) placed at the top of the form/card where the action occurred; entered values are kept. Every data view has loading (`loading-state`, skeleton or "Loading…" with `aria-busy`), empty and error (`error-state` with `retry` button "Retry") states. Buttons disable and show "…" while a request is in flight.
- Dialogs (`confirm-dialog`, role="dialog" aria-modal, width `--width-dialog`, focus trapped, Esc = cancel): title, message, `confirm-yes` (label "Confirm"), `confirm-no` (label "Keep").
- Time formatting: `HH:MM` (24h UTC). Durations: `15 min`. Dates `YYYY-MM-DD`. Counter: `Counter 2`.

## 3. Screens and states

### 3.1 `/customer` — Book (customer)
Purpose: see branches, generate walk-in ticket or book appointment.
- **Desktop 1440×900**: sidebar + content (1200). Top row: page title "Book a visit". Below, a 2-column grid: left (flex 1) list of `branch-card`s (one per active branch: name, address, hours `09:00–17:00`, offered services as chips, `branch-waiting-count` "3 waiting"); right (width `--width-form`) the booking card. Selecting a branch card also sets the form's branch.
- **Mobile 390×844**: single column: booking card first, branch cards below.
- Booking card fields in order: Branch select, Service select (only active services offered by the branch; disabled until branch chosen), mode radio group "Visit type": "Walk-in Queue" / "Scheduled Appointment"; when appointment: Date input and slot grid (3 columns desktop, 2 columns ≤480px); primary button.
- Success (walk-in): the card swaps to `ticket-result` (large mono ticket number, status badge, position, wait, buttons "View My Tickets" → `/customer/tickets` and "Book another"). Success (appointment): toast "Appointment booked for YYYY-MM-DD at HH:MM" and `appointment-result` card with date, time, counter; slot list refreshes.
- Errors via `form-error` using the server message (e.g. closed, duplicate, slot unavailable, past date). Empty: "No branches available" / "No available slots".

### 3.2 `/customer/services`
Read-only list of active services as cards: `service-card` (name, description, `15 min`, category chip). Grid 3 cols desktop, 1 col mobile.

### 3.3 `/customer/tickets` — My Tickets
Auto-refreshes every ≤2 s (polling; no visible flicker; changes announced in an `aria-live="polite"` region `ticket-live`). Two sections: "Active tickets" (`ticket-card`s) and "Upcoming appointments" (`appointment-card`s, status Scheduled). Cards stack, desktop 2-column grid, mobile 1 column. Waiting card: position + estimate. Called card: highlighted left border `--color-status-called`, message "Proceed to counter N". Serving: "Being served at counter N". Empty: "No tickets yet" (`tickets-empty`) with link to Book; "No upcoming appointments".

### 3.4 `/customer/history`
List of `history-row`s newest first: ticket or appointment, number/label, status badge, branch, service, time `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`. Table ≥768px, cards <768px (same testids). Empty: "No history yet".

### 3.5 `/staff` — Queue Desk
- Header strip: `staff-branch` (branch name) and `staff-counter` ("Counter 2").
- **Desktop**: row of 4 stat cards (`staff-waiting-count`, `staff-next`, `staff-completed-today`, `staff-avg-duration`); below, 2 columns: left "Current customer" card (`staff-current`) with action buttons; right "Waiting queue" list.
- **Mobile**: stats in 2×2 grid, current-customer card, then waiting list; action buttons full width stacked, each ≥44px.
- Actions: `btn-call-next` "Call Next" (primary), `btn-start` "Start Service", `btn-complete` "Complete Service", `btn-no-show` "No-Show", `btn-cancel` "Cancel Ticket" (danger outline; opens confirm). Inapplicable buttons are `disabled` and one visible reason is shown in `action-reason` (e.g. "Finish the current customer before calling next", "No waiting customers", "Call a customer first", "Start service first"). Applicable matrix: Call Next ⇔ no Called/Serving ticket and waiting>0; Start ⇔ Called; Complete ⇔ Serving; No-Show ⇔ Called; Cancel ⇔ Called or Serving.
- Staff without a counter: `form-error`-style banner "No counter assigned — ask an admin." and Call Next disabled.
- Empty: `current-empty` "No customer at your counter"; `waiting-empty` "No waiting customers".

### 3.6 `/admin` — Dashboard
- Title "Operations today" + clock controls card: `clock-advance-15` "+15 min", `clock-advance-60` "+60 min", `clock-reset` "Reset clock", showing current app time.
- **Desktop**: stat cards grid 3×3 (`--space-4` gap): Total customers today, Waiting, Called, Serving ("Being served"), Completed, Cancelled, No-Show, Avg waiting time, Avg service duration. Below: two chart cards side by side: "Tickets by status" (horizontal bars, `chart-status`) and "Branch comparison" (grouped bars Completed/Waiting/Cancelled per branch + avg wait/avg service values, `chart-branches`). Each chart has a visible data table (`chart-status-table`, `branch-compare-table`) under it (collapsible `<details>` open by default on desktop, closed on mobile but present in DOM).
- **Mobile**: stat cards 2 columns; charts stacked, bars scale to width, no horizontal overflow.
- Bars use status colours plus text value labels at bar end; chart is SVG/HTML with `role="img"` and `aria-label` summarising values.
- Empty (no tickets today): zeros shown; avg shows `—`. Updates via 2 s polling.

### 3.7 `/admin/monitor`
`monitor-branch-filter` select ("All branches" + branches). List of today's tickets (`monitor-row`): number, branch, service, customer, status badge, counter, staff, created time. Table ≥768px, cards below. Counts line `monitor-count` "11 tickets". Empty "No tickets for this filter". Polls every 2 s.

### 3.8 `/admin/branches`
Table/cards of branches (`branch-row`: name, code, address, hours, counters, services chips, assigned staff names, active badge `Active`/`Inactive`) with `branch-edit` and `branch-add` ("Add branch"). Form shown in a side panel (desktop, width `--width-form`) / full-screen sheet (mobile) with title "Add branch"/"Edit branch".

### 3.9 `/admin/services`
List/cards (`service-row`: name, code, description, `15 min`, category, status badge), `service-add` "Add service", `service-edit`, `service-toggle` ("Deactivate"/"Activate"). Same form container pattern.

### 3.10 `/admin/staff`
List/cards (`staff-row`: name, email, branch, counter `Counter 1` or `Unassigned`), `staff-add` "Add staff", `staff-edit`. Counter assignment is a field in the form.

### 3.11 `/display?branchId=<id>` — Queue display (visitor)
Dark high-contrast screen (`--color-nav-bg` background, white text; text pairs follow the token `nav-text`/`nav-bg`). Header: `display-title` branch name + clock. Left 2/3 "Now calling": grid of `now-calling-item` tiles with ticket number in `--font-size-display` mono and "Counter N" large, Called tiles with ▲ Called and Serving with ● Serving labels. Right 1/3 "Up next": `up-next-item` list of ≥5 next numbers in `--font-size-2xl`. Mobile 360px: single column, display number clamps to 3rem. If `branchId` omitted: `display-branch-select` (label "Branch") shown first. Empty: "No one is being called" / "No waiting tickets". Polls every 2 s.

## 4. Components
- **Button** (`--control-height` 44px, `--radius-md`, medium weight): primary filled teal (hover `--color-primary-hover`), secondary outlined `--color-border-strong`, danger outlined `--color-danger`; disabled: 50% opacity + `not-allowed`; focus ring from tokens.css. Always a `<button>` with visible text label.
- **Field**: visible `<label>` above control, control height 44px, border `--color-border-strong`, radius `--radius-sm`; error text under field in `--color-danger` with `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`; testid `field-error-<field>`.
- **Status badge** (`status-badge`): see §1.
- **Card**: surface, border, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`.
- **Stat card**: label (muted, `--font-size-sm`) over value (`--font-size-2xl` bold).
- **Slot button** (`slot`): 44px, outlined; available = selectable (selected = filled teal, `aria-pressed`); unavailable = disabled with text `HH:MM · Unavailable`.
- **Table → card collapse** below 768px.
- **Toast, form-error, confirm-dialog, loading/empty/error states**: as in §2.
- **Charts**: HTML/SVG bars with text values and table alternative.
- **Side panel/form sheet** for admin entities: focus moves to the first field on open, returns to trigger on close; `Esc` closes.

## 5. Binding test contract
Role access: customer → `/customer*`; staff → `/staff`; admin → `/admin*`; `/display` public. Persona is selected via `persona-switcher` (select; use `selectOption({label})` or value user id) or by setting `localStorage["queueflow.userId"]` before load. Seed ids: customers `usr_201` Alex Rivera, `usr_202` Emma Brown, `usr_203` James Miller; staff `usr_301` Sarah Johnson (Central, counter 1), `usr_302` Michael Chen (Central, counter 2), `usr_303` David Wilson (Downtown, counter 1); admin `usr_401` Jordan Ellis. Branch ids `br_central`, `br_downtown`; service ids `svc_general`, `svc_docs`, `svc_support`. Select option values are entity ids; option text is entity name (service option text is the service name only, e.g. `General Consultation`).

Repeated entities carry `data-id` = entity id (ticket `tkt_…`, appointment `appt_…`, branch/service/user ids) and tickets/rows also `data-number` = ticket number. Locate a ticket by `[data-testid=ticket-card][data-number="CEN-GC-005"]`.

### Shell (all roles)
| testid | element | content |
|---|---|---|
| `persona-switcher` | select, label "Demo account" | options `Name — Role` |
| `current-user` | text | `Emma Brown · Customer` |
| `clock-now` | text | `UTC 10:05` (HH:MM) |
| `nav-*` | links | see §2, label text exact |
| `toast` | role=status | success message |
| `form-error` | role=alert | server/validation message verbatim |
| `field-error-<field>` | text | field validation message |
| `loading-state`, `error-state`, `retry` | | |
| `confirm-dialog`, `confirm-yes` ("Confirm"), `confirm-no` ("Keep") | | |
| `demo-reset` | button "Reset demo data" | opens confirm; confirm resets server state |
| `forbidden-state` | text | access message |

### Customer `/customer`
| testid | element | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branch-card` (data-id) | card | contains `branch-name`, `branch-waiting-count` (text `3 waiting`) |
| `book-branch` | select, label "Branch" | placeholder option value "" "Select a branch" |
| `book-service` | select, label "Service" | placeholder "Select a service" |
| `book-mode-walkin` | radio, label "Walk-in Queue" | default checked |
| `book-mode-appointment` | radio, label "Scheduled Appointment" | reveals date + slots |
| `book-date` | `<input type="date">`, label "Date", `min`=today, `max`=today+14 | default today (app clock) |
| `slot` (data-id=`HH:MM`, `data-available="true|false"`) | button | text `09:00` or `09:30 · Unavailable` (disabled) |
| `slots-empty` | text | "No available slots" |
| `book-submit` | button | label "Generate Ticket" (walk-in) / "Book Appointment" (appointment; disabled until a slot is selected) |
| `ticket-result` | card after walk-in success | contains `ticket-number` (e.g. `CEN-GC-005`), `ticket-status` ("Waiting"), `ticket-position` (`Position 3`), `ticket-wait` (`Est. wait 25 min`) |

Walk-in submit mutates: creates one Waiting ticket (double-click yields one). Appointment submit: creates Scheduled appointment; conflicts show `form-error` with message from API and no appointment is created.

### Customer `/customer/tickets`

### Customer `/customer/history`
`history-row` (data-id, data-number for tickets) contains `history-label` (ticket number or `Appointment`), `history-status` (`Completed|Cancelled|No-Show|Converted`), `history-branch`, `history-service`, `history-time`. Newest first. `history-empty`.

### Customer `/customer/services`
`service-card` (data-id) with `service-name`, `service-duration` (`15 min`), `service-category`, `service-description`.

### Staff `/staff`
`staff-branch` (`Central Branch`), `staff-counter` (`Counter 2`), `staff-waiting-count` (value only, e.g. `2`), `staff-next` (next ticket number or `—`), `staff-completed-today` (integer), `staff-avg-duration` (`13.0 min` or `—`), `staff-current` (card; children `current-ticket-number`, `current-customer`, `current-service`, `current-status` badge), `current-empty`, buttons `btn-call-next`, `btn-start`, `btn-complete`, `btn-no-show`, `btn-cancel` (labels as §3.5), `action-reason`, `waiting-row` (data-id, data-number; children `waiting-number`, `waiting-service`, `waiting-customer`, `waiting-cancel` "Cancel" → confirm), `waiting-empty`. Call Next sets the oldest Waiting ticket at the branch to Called and fills `staff-current`; `form-error` shows API message on conflicts (`STAFF_BUSY`, `QUEUE_EMPTY`, `NO_COUNTER` messages). Seeds: Sarah Johnson (counter 1) serving CEN-GC-002; Michael Chen serving CEN-CS-001 — both must Complete before Call Next is enabled.

### Admin `/admin`
Stat values (testid on the value element, text exact): `stat-total`, `stat-waiting`, `stat-called`, `stat-serving`, `stat-completed`, `stat-cancelled`, `stat-no-show` (integers) and `stat-avg-wait`, `stat-avg-service` (`13.8 min` / `11.3 min`; `—` if none). Seed values: 11, 3, 0, 3, 3, 1, 1, 13.8 min, 11.3 min. `chart-status` (role=img) + `chart-status-table` (rows `status-row` data-id=status key with `status-row-count`); `chart-branches` + `branch-compare-table` (`branch-compare-row` data-id=branch id with `compare-completed`, `compare-waiting`, `compare-cancelled`, `compare-avg-wait`, `compare-avg-service`). ### Admin `/admin/monitor`
`monitor-branch-filter` (value "" = All branches), `monitor-count`, `monitor-row` (data-id, data-number) with `monitor-number`, `monitor-status`, `monitor-counter` (`Counter 1` or `—`), `monitor-staff` (name or `—`), `monitor-branch`, `monitor-service`.

### Admin `/admin/branches`
`branch-row` (data-id) with `branch-row-name`, `branch-row-code`, `branch-row-address`, `branch-row-hours` (`09:00–17:00`), `branch-row-counters` (integer), `branch-row-services`, `branch-row-staff`, `branch-row-status`; `branch-add`, `branch-edit`. Errors: `field-error-name|code|address|openTime|counterCount|serviceIds`, and `form-error` for API conflicts (e.g. `COUNTER_IN_USE`). Success: panel closes, toast "Branch saved", row updated/added.

### Admin `/admin/services`
`service-row` (data-id) with `service-row-name`, `service-row-code`, `service-row-duration` (`15 min`), `service-row-category`, `service-row-status` (`Active`/`Inactive`); `service-add`, `service-edit`, `service-toggle`. Form `service-form`: `service-name`, `service-code`, `service-description` (textarea), `service-duration-input` (`type=number` min 1 max 240, label "Duration (minutes)"), `service-category`, `service-active` (checkbox), `service-save` ("Save service"), `service-cancel`. Toast "Service saved". (Note `service-name`/`service-duration` on the customer services page are output elements; form inputs use the names above.)

### Admin `/admin/staff`
`staff-row` (data-id) with `staff-row-name`, `staff-row-email`, `staff-row-branch`, `staff-row-counter` (`Counter 1` / `Unassigned`); `staff-add`, `staff-edit`. Form `staff-form`: `staff-form-name`, `staff-form-email` (`type=email`), `staff-form-branch` (select, option value = branch id), `staff-form-counter` (select; options "" = "Unassigned" and `1`…`N` for selected branch, labels `Counter 1`…), `staff-form-save` ("Save staff"), `staff-form-cancel`. API conflicts (`COUNTER_TAKEN`) appear in `form-error`; toast "Staff saved".

### Display `/display?branchId=br_central`
`display-branch-select` (only without branchId), `display-title`, `now-calling-item` (data-id) with `display-ticket-number`, `display-counter` (`Counter 2`), `display-status`; `up-next-item` with `display-next-number`; `display-empty-calling`, `display-empty-next`.

### Derived edge/smoke contracts

- Closed branch / inactive service: `form-error` with API message; inactive services are absent from `book-service` options.
- Past date: `book-date` has `min`=today; if bypassed the API error shows in `form-error`.
- Smoke: every route in §2 renders without console errors, without horizontal overflow at 360px and 390px, with persona `usr_*` of the proper role.

## 6. Visual evidence plan
`visual-plan.json` has three targets, captured at 1440×900 and 390×844:
1. **primary** — `/customer/tickets` as Emma Brown after generating a Central/General Consultation walk-in ticket. Ready when a `ticket-card` with `CEN-GC-NNN`, `Waiting`, position and wait is visible. Criteria: badge icon+text, clear ticket number hierarchy, position/wait readable, nav usable, no overflow.
2. **staff-desk** — `/staff` as Michael Chen at seed: current customer card with enabled Complete, disabled buttons with reason, waiting list, stat cards. Criteria: action buttons ≥44px, disabled reason visible, stat cards aligned.
3. **admin-dashboard** — `/admin` as Jordan Ellis: stat cards and both charts. Criteria: values legible, bars with text labels and table alternative, 2-column mobile cards without clipping.

## 7. Assumptions and limitations
- Persona switcher without passwords is the explicit demo authentication boundary; no real login.
- Real-time uses 2 s polling; the UI never needs manual refresh.
- Contrast pairs are selected to target WCAG AA but not measured here.
- Charts are simple HTML/SVG (no chart package may be installed).
- Admin entities cannot be deleted (per requirements); deactivate via `service-toggle` / `branch-active`.
- Branch-level queue is FIFO across services; no priority lanes.
- Ticket `data-number` may repeat across business days; tests use today's tickets only.

`npm run build` passes and `npx vitest run` passes (6 files, 42 tests). I never ran the app, so none of the API or UI behaviour has been exercised.

I tried a one-off `tsx` script to walk the primary journey through the server services. The shell refused it, so I did not retry. The journey, the appointment conversion and the role checks therefore have no runtime verification. I did not run Playwright, and I did not read or write `e2e/` or capture any screenshots.

**Built**
- **Server:** one router and one service per resource, covering every endpoint in the requirements contract.
  - `X-User-Id` is checked on every call: 401 for an unknown ID, 403 for the wrong role.
  - Error responses use the `{error:{code,message,fields?}}` shape.
  - `Cache-Control: no-store` is set on all API responses.
  - Due appointments convert to tickets on every request and on a 5 s timer.
  - The demo clock is persisted in the store (real-time start plus advanced minutes), and `POST /api/reset` restores the seed.
